reader.requirement: At --std 85, the implementor must define the size of a data transfer for each hardware device ACCEPT reaches, and the compiler must transfer that size: WiseOwl documents one 80-character record for every input device (CONSOLE, SYSIN and the FROM-omitted default), a shorter line padded and a longer line split into consecutive records (DOC-A.1-5).
reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior in AcceptDisplayEmitter.cs, AcceptSource.cs and ReceivingStore.cs: no hit; the conversion form is the --numeric-display compile option, not the edition (DOC-A.1-1: 'at every --std').
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_z08 covers elementary alphanumeric receivers; not exercised: a COMP receiver (one whole record) and a receiver spanning three records

probes.expected: a 90-character line is two 80-character records, the second padded; X(170) takes both and requests a third record (WXYZ) for its last 10 positions
a COMP receiver converts one whole record (DOC-A.1-1, DOC-A.1-5)

probes.printed: run with empty input: every receiver spaces, 7[000.00]
probes.expected: end of input leaves spaces, converting to zero (DOC-A.1-5)

reader.notes: The size is the implementor's, documented in docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-5.md and implemented by the one constant AcceptSource.RecordSize for every device. Input runs used the run_probe-built program with input redirected (acc_size.in, acc_size2.in), as for GR1.

refuter.evidence: The size is the implementor's (DOC-A.1-5: one 80-character record for every input device; output-only devices are refused for ACCEPT, so they need no input size). Probe acc_lines (CRLF input, runs/acc_lines-001, run with acc_lines.in redirected): a 100-character line into X(10) keeps 0123456789 and the next ACCEPT Y(10) starts at the NEXT line (NEXTLINE01), as DOC-A.1-5 says; a 100-character line into X(100) takes record 1 (80) plus 20 characters of record 2; CRLF terminators never reach the receiver; '42' into PIC 9(3) is 042. The behaviour matches the documented size at every case tried. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.5.4 GR2  (6.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2'.
